sentences.text: TTCN-3 variables are statically typed variables.
Variables are either value variables to store values or template variables to store templates.

Variables can be of simple basic types, basic string types, structured types, special data types (including subtypes derived from these types) as well as address, component or default, port or timer types.
The type of the variable is either provided explicitly or implicitly according to the rules for automatic typing specified in clause 6.5.

When automatic typing is used, the TypeOrNestedParDef part of the declaration is missing and the type of the variable is equal to the type of the expression or template body on the right-hand side of the assignment.
Variables can be declared and used in test cases, functions and altsteps.
Additionally, variables can be declared in component type definitions.
These variables can be used in test cases, altsteps and functions which are running on a given component type.
Variables can be declared lazy using the @lazy modifier.
Alternatively, variables can be declared fuzzy using the @fuzzy modifier.

If a variable is declared fuzzy or lazy they can additionally declared with the @deterministic modifier to indicate that when used in a deterministic evaluation context, any evaluation of the variable would have no side effect and would yield the same result.
Lazy and fuzzy features are valid only in the scope, where the variables' names are visible.
For example, if a fuzzy variable is passed to a formal parameter declared without a modifier, it loses its fuzzy feature inside the called function.
Similarly, if it is passed to a lazy formal parameter, it becomes lazy within the called function.

Whenever a lazy or fuzzy variable is assigned, the TE is required to save the lexical environment (the set of directly or indirectly referenced values and templates) valid at the time of the assignment, so that it is possible to resolve the expression at the time of evaluation of the lazy or fuzzy value or template.
If the assignment was made on a lower scope than the evaluation, saving the lexical environment extends lifetime of the referenced variables defined on that lower scope.
A TTCN-3 value variable stores values.
It is declared by the var keyword followed by a type identifier or a nested type definition and a variable identifier.
An initial value can be assigned at variable declaration.

It may be used at the right hand side as well as at the left hand side of assignments, in expressions, following the return keyword in bodies of functions with a return clause in their headers and may be passed to both value and template-type formal parameters.

var [ ( @lazy | @fuzzy ) [ @deterministic ] ] [ TypeOrNestedTypeDef ]
   { VarIdentifier [ ArrayDef ] [ ":=" Expression ] [ "," ] }+ [ ";" ]
A value variable associates a name with the location of a value.
A value variable may change its value during test execution several times.
A value can be assigned several times to a value variable.
The value variable can be referenced multiple times in a TTCN-3 module.
In addition to the general static rules of TTCN-3 given in clause 5, the following restrictions apply:
a) _Expression shall evaluate to a value which is type compatible with TypeOrNestedTypeDef._ b) Value variables shall store values only.
c) Value variables shall not be declared or used in a module definitions part (i.e. global variables are not supported in TTCN-3).
d) Use of uninitialized value variables at other places than the left hand side of assignments, in return statements, or as actual parameters passed to formal parameters shall cause an error.
e) The initialization or assignment of a fuzzy or lazy variable shall not contain function calls of functions with inout or out parameters.
The called functions may use other functions with inout or out parameters internally.

f) If a lazy or fuzzy value variable is used in deterministic contexts (i.e. during the evaluation of a snapshot or initialization of global non-fuzzy templates), it shall be declared @deterministic and the expression assigned to the variable shall fulfill the restrictions imposed on content of functions used in special places given in clause 16.1.4.
g) The expression assigned to a lazy or fuzzy variable might contain a direct or indirect reference to this variable.
Evaluation of such an expression shall cause a dynamic error.

h) Using the dot notation (see clauses 6.2.1.1, 6.2.2.1 and 6.2.5.1) and index notation (see clauses 6.2.7 and 6.2.3.0) for referencing a field, alternative or element of an address value, which actual value is null shall cause an error.
i) The expression shall evaluate to a value, which is at least partially initialized.
j) If the TypeOrNestedTypeDef part is missing from the declaration, the ArrayDef part shall be missing as well and the assignment part (i.e. ":=" Expression) shall be present.
A TTCN-3 template variable stores templates.
They are declared by the `var template` keyword followed by a type identifier and a variable identifier.
An initial content can be assigned at declaration.
In addition to values, template variables may also store matching mechanisms (see clause 15.6.6).

Template variables may be used on the right hand side as well as on the left hand side of assignments, following the `return` keyword in bodies of functions defining a template-type return value in their headers and may be passed as actual parameters to template-type formal parameters.
It is also allowed to assign a template instance to a template variable or a template variable field.

var TemplateModifier [ (@lazy | @fuzzy) [ @deterministic ] ]
   [ TypeOrNestedTypeDef ] { VarIdentifier [ ArrayDef ] ":=" TemplateBody [ "," ] }+ [ ";" ]
A template variable associates a name with the location of a template or a value (as every value is also a template).
A template variable may change its template during test execution several times.
A template or value can be assigned several times to a template variable.
The template variable can be referenced multiple times in a TTCN-3 module.
The content of a template variable can be restricted to the matching mechanisms specific value and omit in the same way as formal template parameters, see clause 5.4.1.2.
The restriction template (omit) can be replaced by the shorthand notation omit.
NOTE 1: String and list type templates can be concatenated, see clause 15.11.
In addition to the general static rules of TTCN-3 given in clause 5, the following restrictions apply:
a) Template variables shall not be declared or used in a module definitions part (i.e. global variables are not supported in TTCN-3).

b) When used on the right hand side of assignments template variables shall not be operands of TTCN-3 operators (see clause 7.1) and the variable on the left hand side shall be a template variable too.
c) When accessing element of template variables either on the left hand side or on the right hand side of assignments, the rules given in clause 15.6 shall apply.
NOTE 2: While it is not allowed to directly apply TTCN-3 operations to template variables, it is allowed to use the dot notation and the index notation to inspect and modify template variable fields.
d) Use of uninitialized template variables at other places than the left hand side of assignments, in return statements, or as actual parameters passed to formal parameters shall cause an error.
e) Void.
f) If the template variable is restricted, then the template used to initialize it shall contain only the matching mechanisms as described in clause 15.8.
g) Template variables, similarly to global and local templates, shall be fully specified in order to be used in sending and receiving operations.
h) Restrictions on templates in clause 15.0 shall apply.
i) The initialization or assignment of a fuzzy or lazy variable shall not contain function calls of functions with inout or out parameters.
The called functions may use other functions with inout or out parameters internally.

j) If a lazy or fuzzy template variable is used in deterministic contexts (i.e. during the evaluation of a snapshot or initialization of global non-fuzzy templates), it shall be declared @deterministic and the template body assigned to the variable shall fulfill the restrictions imposed on content of functions used in special places given in clause 16.1.4.

k) Using the dot notation (see clauses 6.2.1.1, 6.2.2.1 and 6.2.5.1) and index notation (see clause 6.2.7) for referencing a field, alternative or element of an address value, which actual value is null shall cause an error.
l) The template body at the right-hand side of the assignment symbol shall evaluate to a value or template, which is type compatible with the variable being declared.
m) The template body at the right-hand side of the assignment symbol shall evaluate to an object that is at least partially initialized.
n) If the TypeOrNestedTypeDef part is missing from the declaration, the ArrayDef part shall be missing as well and the assignment part (i.e. ":=" TemplateBody) shall be present.

requirements.condition: the template variable is used on the right hand side of an assignment
requirements.canonical: If a template variable is used on the right hand side of an assignment, the variable on the left hand side SHALL be a template variable.
requirements.original: b) When used on the right hand side of assignments template variables shall not be operands of TTCN-3 operators (see clause 7.1) and the variable on the left hand side shall be a template variable too.

readings: If a template variable is used on the right hand side of an assignment, the variable on the left hand side SHALL be a template variable.

If a template variable is used on the right hand side of an assignment, the target on the left hand side SHALL be a template variable or a field of a template variable (e.g. accessed via dot or index notation).
ambiguity.issue: 'the variable on the left hand side' does not say whether a field or element of a template variable counts; the second reading is consistent with 11.2-s006, the first is the literal reading and is chosen.

requirements.subject: ent:template-variable
requirements.condition: an element of a template variable is accessed in an assignment
requirements.canonical: When an element of a template variable is accessed on the left hand side or the right hand side of an assignment, the rules of clause 15.6 SHALL apply.
requirements.original: c) When accessing element of template variables either on the left hand side or on the right hand side of assignments, the rules given in clause 15.6 shall apply.

requirements.subject: ent:template-variable
requirements.canonical: The dot notation and the index notation MAY be used to inspect and modify fields of a template variable, although TTCN-3 operations SHALL NOT be applied directly to template variables.
requirements.original: NOTE 2: While it is not allowed to directly apply TTCN-3 operations to template variables, it is allowed to use the dot notation and the index notation to inspect and modify template variable fields.

ambiguity.issue: The NOTE says 'TTCN-3 operations' while restriction b) it explains speaks of 'TTCN-3 operators (see clause 7.1)'.

requirements.subject: ent:uninitialized-variable
requirements.canonical: Use of an uninitialized template variable at any place other than the left hand side of an assignment, a return statement, or an actual parameter passed to a formal parameter SHALL cause an error.
requirements.original: d) Use of uninitialized template variables at other places than the left hand side of assignments, in return statements, or as actual parameters passed to formal parameters shall cause an error.

readings: Use of an uninitialized template variable in any other place SHALL cause an error (static or dynamic).
Use of an uninitialized template variable in any other place SHALL cause a dynamic error at runtime only.
ambiguity.issue: The kind of error (compile-time or runtime) is not stated; since template variable declarations require an initial TemplateBody, it is also unclear how a template variable can be uninitialized. The generic reading is chosen.

requirements.subject: ent:template-restriction
requirements.condition: the template variable has a template restriction
requirements.canonical: If a template variable is restricted, the template used to initialize it SHALL contain only the matching mechanisms permitted by the restriction as described in clause 15.8.
requirements.original: f) If the template variable is restricted, then the template used to initialize it shall contain only the matching mechanisms as described in clause 15.8.

requirements.subject: ent:template-variable
requirements.condition: the template variable is used in a sending or receiving operation
requirements.canonical: A template variable SHALL be completely initialized in order to be used in a sending or receiving operation, as global and local templates.
requirements.original: g) Template variables, similarly to global and local templates, shall be fully specified in order to be used in sending and receiving operations.

ambiguity.issue: 'fully specified' is not a defined term; the glossary term 'completely initialized' is meant. For sending operations the template additionally has to resolve to a value (clause 15.0).

requirements.subject: ent:template-variable
requirements.canonical: The restrictions on templates given in clause 15.0 SHALL apply to template variables.
requirements.original: h) Restrictions on templates in clause 15.0 shall apply.

requirements.subject: ent:lazy-variable
requirements.canonical: The initialization or assignment of a lazy or fuzzy template variable SHALL NOT contain a call of a function with `inout` or `out` parameters.
requirements.original: i) The initialization or assignment of a fuzzy or lazy variable shall not contain function calls of functions with inout or out parameters.

requirements.subject: ent:function
requirements.canonical: A function called in the initialization or assignment of a lazy or fuzzy template variable MAY internally call other functions with `inout` or `out` parameters.
requirements.original: The called functions may use other functions with inout or out parameters internally.

requirements.subject: ent:deterministic-modifier
requirements.condition: a lazy or fuzzy template variable is used in a deterministic context
requirements.canonical: If a lazy or fuzzy template variable is used in a deterministic context (i.e. during the evaluation of a snapshot or the initialization of a global non-fuzzy template), the variable SHALL be declared `@deterministic`.
requirements.original: j) If a lazy or fuzzy template variable is used in deterministic contexts (i.e. during the evaluation of a snapshot or initialization of global non-fuzzy templates), it shall be declared @deterministic and the template body assigned to the variable shall fulfill the restrictions imposed on content of functions used in special places given in clause 16.1.4.

requirements.subject: ent:template-body
requirements.condition: a lazy or fuzzy template variable is used in a deterministic context
requirements.canonical: If a lazy or fuzzy template variable is used in a deterministic context, the template body assigned to the variable SHALL fulfil the restrictions on the content of functions used in special places given in clause 16.1.4.
requirements.original: j) If a lazy or fuzzy template variable is used in deterministic contexts (i.e. during the evaluation of a snapshot or initialization of global non-fuzzy templates), it shall be declared @deterministic and the template body assigned to the variable shall fulfill the restrictions imposed on content of functions used in special places given in clause 16.1.4.

requirements.subject: ent:address-value
requirements.condition: the actual value of the address value is `null` (in the context of template variables)
requirements.canonical: Using the dot notation or the index notation to reference a field, alternative or element of an address value whose actual value is `null` SHALL cause an error.
requirements.original: k) Using the dot notation (see clauses 6.2.1.1, 6.2.2.1 and 6.2.5.1) and index notation (see clause 6.2.7) for referencing a field, alternative or element of an address value, which actual value is null shall cause an error.

requirements.subject: ent:template-body
requirements.canonical: The template body on the right-hand side of the assignment symbol in a template variable declaration SHALL evaluate to a value or template that is type compatible with the declared template variable.
requirements.original: l) The template body at the right-hand side of the assignment symbol shall evaluate to a value or template, which is type compatible with the variable being declared.

requirements.subject: ent:template-body
requirements.canonical: The template body on the right-hand side of the assignment symbol in a template variable declaration SHALL evaluate to an object that is at least partially initialized.
requirements.original: m) The template body at the right-hand side of the assignment symbol shall evaluate to an object that is at least partially initialized.

requirements.subject: ent:template-variable-declaration
requirements.condition: the TypeOrNestedTypeDef part is missing
requirements.canonical: If the TypeOrNestedTypeDef part is missing from a template variable declaration, the ArrayDef part SHALL be missing as well.
requirements.original: n) If the TypeOrNestedTypeDef part is missing from the declaration, the ArrayDef part shall be missing as well and the assignment part (i.e. ":=" TemplateBody) shall be present.

requirements.subject: ent:template-variable-declaration
requirements.condition: the TypeOrNestedTypeDef part is missing
requirements.canonical: If the TypeOrNestedTypeDef part is missing from a template variable declaration, the assignment part (":=" TemplateBody) SHALL be present.
requirements.original: n) If the TypeOrNestedTypeDef part is missing from the declaration, the ArrayDef part shall be missing as well and the assignment part (i.e. ":=" TemplateBody) shall be present.

requirements.subject: ent:fuzzy-variable
requirements.canonical: A fuzzy template variable IS evaluated on every usage.
requirements.original: var template @fuzzy float v_fuzzTemp1 := rnd(); // evaluated on every usage

non_requirement.reason: introduces the restrictions list of 11.1 and refers to the general static rules of clause 5
introduces the restrictions list of 11.2 and refers to the general static rules of clause 5
